chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muawiya ibn Hukeym, from Abu Shuayb al-Mahamili al-Rafaiy who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who agreed with another man to dig a well for him ten statures deep for ten dirhams. So he dug one stature for him, then was unable to continue. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ten (dirhams) are divided into fifty-five parts. Whatever one part he receives is for the first stature, two parts for the second, and three parts for the third, according to this calculation up to ten.'
ai.seo_question: How is payment divided when a worker completes only part of a fixed-depth well-digging contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the application of proportional compensation in fixed-price contracts (iqti'a) when work is partially completed, utilizing a unique arithmetic progression where shares increase with each unit (1 to 10 parts out of 55). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in labor agreements, ensuring that the worker is rewarded not just linearly but in a manner that accounts for the cumulative effort or value of each completed segment. This ruling underscores the practical legal reasoning (fiqh) developed by the Imams to resolve specific economic disputes within the community.
